verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft and its four-astronaut crew are in space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'A towering orange-and-white NASA rocket blasted off from Florida on Wednesday evening, lifting four astronauts toward space'; R3: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'NASA’s SLS rocket lifted off from Launch Pad 39B at 6:35 p.m. EDT Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm successful launch on April 1, 2026, placing spacecraft and crew in space post-liftoff.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission had a successful liftoff at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the powerful rocket launched into the clear sky at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time'; R3: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'lifted off from Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Exact details of time, location, and success match across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is executing a 10-day journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'what is expected to be a round trip of more than 695,000 miles'; R2: 'over the course of about a 10-day mission'; R3: 'The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R6: 'an approximately 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is moving away from the upper stage of the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The proximity operations have concluded. The crew in their Orion capsule will move away from the upper stage'; 'Orion spacecraft separated from the upper stage of the rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Source directly states separation and moving away after proximity operations.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is beginning its trajectory toward the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Thursday, Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon'; R6: 'mission controllers will give Orion’s... command to conduct the translunar injection burn on Thursday, April 2'
verifications.reasoning: As of April 1 post-launch, mission is in Earth orbit; trajectory to Moon (TLI) begins April 2.

verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission's location is in transit to the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'placed the spacecraft in a large looping orbit that swung out more than 43,000 miles'; 'On Thursday, Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon'; R3: 'prepare the spacecraft for deep‑space operations' (post-SAWs on April 1); R6: 'translunar injection burn on Thursday, April 2'
verifications.reasoning: On April 1, still in high Earth orbit, not yet in transit to Moon (pre-TLI).

verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission is departing low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'two firings of the upper stage of the rocket that placed the spacecraft in a large looping orbit that swung out more than 43,000 miles'; R3: 'PRM (perigee raise maneuver) and ARB (apogee raise burn) that will increase the lowest and highest points'; R6: 'upper stage fired to put Orion into an elliptical orbit around Earth. A second planned burn... into a high Earth orbit extending about 46,000 miles'
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch on April 1, upper stage burns transition from LEO to high Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: Solar array wings (SAWs) have successfully deployed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The Orion spacecraft’s SAWs (solar arrays wings) have fully deployed, completing a key configuration step... all four wings unfolded as planned, locking into place'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of successful SAW deployment post-launch on April 1.

verifications.claim: Solar array wings (SAWs) are generating power for the Orion capsule named Integrity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'beginning to draw power... Each wing has 15,000 solar cells to convert sunlight to electricity'; 'Orion, named Integrity'
verifications.reasoning: Source confirms power generation by SAWs for named capsule Integrity.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The proximity operations have concluded. The crew in their Orion capsule will move away from the upper stage'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit statement that proximity operations concluded post-separation.

verifications.claim: The crew is performing a 10-day test flight to test systems for future moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Like Apollo 8, Artemis II aims to check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey'; R2: 'confirm all of the spacecraft’s systems operate as designed... pave the way to land... on Artemis III'; R6: 'demonstrate life support systems... lay the foundation for an enduring presence on the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe as test flight validating systems for future lunar missions.

verifications.claim: The goal of the Artemis II mission is to circumnavigate the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'a journey that will take astronauts around the moon but not land there'; R2: 'pave the way for long-term return to the Moon'; R4: 'journey around the moon'; R6: 'test flight around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent description as lunar flyby/circumnavigation without landing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed mission to circumnavigate the Moon in over 50 years
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972. “After a brief 54-year intermission'; R6: 'first crewed lunar flyby in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed deep space/lunar mission in 50+ years since Apollo.
